# Controls

27 controls: 21 `implemented`, 3 `procedural`, 2 `planned`, 1 `not-applicable`.

**A green check means the evidence resolves, not that it is sufficient.** `yarn lint:docs` proves that each anchor below exists at HEAD: the symbol is declared, the test title is present and not skipped in a tier a pull-request workflow runs, the workflow job exists and runs the named command, the heading is there. It does not prove that a test asserts what its control claims, that a threshold is right, or that a mapping to a clause is the best one. Those are judgements, and each sits beside its evidence so a reader can disagree with it.

**Coverage is not claimed.** The check asserts that every catalogued control has evidence, not that every clause of a framework has a control. Each framework section below says how many of its clauses no control here addresses.

† The ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A identifiers, titles and the count of 38 are taken from secondary sources — ISMS.online, "ISO 42001 Annex A Controls Explained" (https://www.isms.online/iso-42001/annex-a-controls/), and RiskProfs, "ISO 42001 Annex A Controls List: All 38 Controls Explained" (https://riskprofs.com/iso-42001-annex-a-controls-list/), which agree — and were not checked against the standard's text. A reader with the standard can correct them.

| Status           | Means                                                                   |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `implemented`    | A test or a CI job fails if the control stops holding.                  |
| `procedural`     | A person enforces it by applying a written rule. No check does.         |
| `planned`        | Not delivered. The owner is the PRD that delivers it.                   |
| `not-applicable` | Excluded, with the justification a Statement of Applicability requires. |

Every run on either graph, every prior-authorization recommendation and every clinician's signed determination is appended to a hash chain of salted commitments, written by ledger_writer, a role with SELECT and INSERT only; ledger:verify re-derives each run's digest from its record and checkpoints and checks every signature against reviewer keys that are themselves entries. A superuser in replica mode can still rewrite the database, so RFC 3161 anchors are what detect a rewrite, and only at or before the last anchor; scheduling anchors, archiving tokens and reviewer-key custody are a deployment's. The repository holds no ePHI (ADR 0003), so the §164.312 mappings describe the safeguard's shape, not a compliance obligation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| CTL-AUD-02  | Every run's inputs and decisions are recorded, and a replay proves the record complete against its checkpoints                                                                  | `implemented`    | AI RMF MEASURE 2.4; ISO/IEC 42001 A.6.2.8†; §164.312 (b)                     | [`RunRecorder`](../apps/agent-service/src/audit/run-recorder.ts); [`replayRun`](../apps/agent-service/src/audit/replay-run.ts); test [`'leaves one run_records row holding the body sent and every decision in order'`](../apps/agent-service/test/audit-replay.integration.test.ts) (integration); test [`'replays a stub run with every checkpoint matching, and derives what it wrote'`](../apps/agent-service/test/audit-replay.integration.test.ts) (integration); test [`'editing one checkpoint blob exits 1 at that step'`](../apps/agent-service/test/audit-replay.integration.test.ts) (integration); test [`'answers 503 and returns no decision when the assessment cannot be recorded'`](../apps/agent-service/src/fhir/prior-auth.service.test.ts) (unit); [`e2e.yml`](../.github/workflows/e2e.yml) job `e2e`, runs `yarn turbo test:integration` — on pull_request, workflow_dispatch; Delivered by P3-B (ADR 0007). The record holds the request, the commit, the models and every decision at the cassette seam plus memory.retrieve, appended as each resolves; audit:replay re-executes the run at its commit and compares every checkpoint. It proves the record complete and consistent, not unaltered — a consistent edit to a record and its checkpoints passes, and detecting one is CTL-AUD-01. The prior-authorization path fails closed when a record cannot be written; the chat path fails open and closes the record partial. The §164.312 mapping describes the safeguard's shape; the repository holds no ePHI (ADR 0003).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| CTL-AUD-03  | Before real member data, run records and checkpoints are encrypted at rest, read-logged, read through a separate role and retained to the record-keeping floor                  | `procedural`     | AI RMF MEASURE 2.10; §164.312 (a)(1), (b)                                    | [`.context/conventions.md`](../.context/conventions.md) § Before real data; Written by P3-B. The deploying covered entity owns every item, and no test in this repository can evidence a deployment's configuration. Nothing here deletes a run record or a checkpoint, by decision; a prune built later must be a ledger event (P3-C). On the replay axis the inference spans carry recorded usage and are marked agent_native.replayed, so they are not a measurement of the current model. Content capture is off, and opt-in capture is P3-C's.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| CTL-COST-01 | A trial is bounded in input tokens, output tokens and model calls, asserted in CI                                                                                               | `implemented`    | OWASP LLM10:2025                                                             | [`checkBudgets`](../packages/eval-harness/src/budgets.ts); test [`'keeps a correct trial that spent too much passed, and counts the breach beside the rate'`](../packages/eval-harness/src/harness.test.ts) (unit); test [`'ends failed on a budget breach although every trial passed'`](../apps/agent-service/src/eval/run-suite.test.ts) (unit); [`agent-eval.yml`](../.github/workflows/agent-eval.yml) job `replay`, runs `yarn eval` — on pull_request, push, schedule, workflow_dispatch; Delivered by P1-F. Each task file sets per-trial ceilings, checked against the trial's own inference spans beside the graders, so a breach fails the run without moving the pass rate. On the replay job a budget checks the committed cassettes, so it fails on a re-recording that costs more and on nothing else; the nightly live job checks a fresh sample once a repository secret exists. Latency and an estimated dollar cost are reported and not asserted. A latency budget is rejected outright; a dollar assertion waits for two model ids with different prices, which P1-E compares. modelCalls counts operations, not HTTP requests, so a client's own retries inside one call are bounded by P1-C's 429 classifier, not here.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| CTL-ACC-01  | Every request to the external surface, except discovery and health, is authenticated                                                                                            | `implemented`    | OWASP ASI03; §164.312 (d)                                                    | [`docs/adr/0014-service-authentication-bearer-at-the-service-open-when-unconfigured.md`](../docs/adr/0014-service-authentication-bearer-at-the-service-open-when-unconfigured.md) § Decision; [`requireCredential`](../apps/agent-service/src/auth/require-credential.ts); test [`'answers 401 with a Bearer challenge to a missing token'`](../apps/agent-service/test/auth.e2e-spec.ts) (service); test [`'answers 401 with a Bearer challenge to a wrong token'`](../apps/agent-service/test/auth.e2e-spec.ts) (service); test [`'covers a route nobody named, because the rule is deny by default'`](../apps/agent-service/test/auth.e2e-spec.ts) (service); test [`'exits 1 within two seconds naming SERVICE_CREDENTIALS when it is malformed'`](../apps/agent-service/test/boot.e2e-spec.ts) (service); [`ci.yml`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml) job `ci`, runs `yarn turbo test:service` — on pull_request, push; [`e2e.yml`](../.github/workflows/e2e.yml) job `browser-e2e` — on pull_request, workflow_dispatch; Delivered by P5-A. A bearer token, checked at the service because compose publishes the service's port, against sha256 digests in SERVICE_CREDENTIALS. Deny by default, so /runs, /a2a, /fhir and /review are covered without being named; GET /health and the two /.well-known documents are exempt. Unset runs open with auth.open at warn, which is the repository's axis rule and is stated in the Agent Card by declaring no security; the compose stack runs authenticated. The §164.312 mapping describes the safeguard's shape; the repository holds no ePHI (ADR 0003).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| CTL-ACC-02  | An A2A caller reaches only the tasks and conversations it created                                                                                                               | `implemented`    | OWASP ASI03; §164.312 (a)(1)                                                 | [`contextSessionId`](../apps/agent-service/src/a2a/session-id.ts); test [`'does not show principal a's task to principal b'`](../apps/agent-service/test/a2a.e2e-spec.ts) (service); test [`'gives two principals in one context two sessions'`](../apps/agent-service/src/a2a/session-id.test.ts) (unit); [`e2e.yml`](../.github/workflows/e2e.yml) job `browser-e2e` — on pull_request, workflow_dispatch; Delivered by P5-A. Tasks live in the SDK's owner-scoped store keyed by the authenticated principal, so another principal's GetTask is -32001 and its ListTasks omits them. A context's session id is UUIDv5 over principal and context, so the same context id from two principals is two conversations; the compose job checks that against live memory. Not covered, and stated in ADR 0014 as a residual, is POST /runs, whose contract lets an authenticated caller name any session. In open mode every caller is one principal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| CTL-ACC-03  | Traffic to the service is encrypted in transit                                                                                                                                  | `not-applicable` | §164.312 (e)(1)                                                              | Rationale: Nothing in this repository is deployed, and TLS terminates at the deploying organization's ingress, outside the code here. A2A §7.1 makes HTTPS a MUST in production, so a deployment that serves real callers must put one in front of the gateway. The repository holds synthetic data only (ADR 0003). ## Frameworks

### NIST AI 100-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)

Registry id `nist-ai-rmf-1.0`, edition of 2023-01. Source: <https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1>.

**15 of 72 subcategories referenced; 57 not assessed.** Subcategory text copied from Tables 1–4 of the NIST PDF (GOVERN 19, MAP 18, MEASURE 22, MANAGE 13).

| Clause       | Text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Controls                              |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| GOVERN 1.4   | The risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | CTL-DOC-01                            |
| GOVERN 3.2   | Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | CTL-HUM-01, CTL-HUM-02, CTL-HUM-03    |
| GOVERN 4.3   | Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | CTL-LOG-01                            |
| MAP 3.5      | Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the GOVERN function.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | CTL-HUM-01, CTL-HUM-02                |
| MAP 4.1      | Approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of its components – including the use of third-party data or software – are in place, followed, and documented, as are risks of infringement of a third party's intellectual property or other rights.                                                                                                                                                                        | CTL-DATA-01, CTL-DATA-02              |
| MEASURE 1.1  | Approaches and metrics for measurement of AI risks enumerated during the MAP function are selected for implementation starting with the most significant AI risks. The risks or trustworthiness characteristics that will not – or cannot – be measured are properly documented.                                                                                                                                                   | CTL-EVAL-02                           |
| MEASURE 2.3  | AI system performance or assurance criteria are measured qualitatively or quantitatively and demonstrated for conditions similar to deployment setting(s). Measures are documented.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | CTL-EVAL-01, CTL-EVAL-03, CTL-EVAL-04 |
| MEASURE 2.4  | The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components – as identified in the MAP function – are monitored when in production.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | CTL-EVAL-05, CTL-AUD-02, CTL-OBS-01   |
| MEASURE 2.5  | The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be valid and reliable. Limitations of the generalizability beyond the conditions under which the technology was developed are documented.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | CTL-EVAL-01                           |
| MEASURE 2.6  | The AI system is evaluated regularly for safety risks – as identified in the MAP function. The AI system to be deployed is demonstrated to be safe, its residual negative risk does not exceed the risk tolerance, and it can fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits. Safety metrics reflect system reliability and robustness, real-time monitoring, and response times for AI system failures. | CTL-RES-01                            |
| MEASURE 2.7  | AI system security and resilience – as identified in the MAP function – are evaluated and documented.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | CTL-SEC-01                            |
| MEASURE 2.10 | Privacy risk of the AI system – as identified in the MAP function – is examined and documented.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | CTL-DATA-01, CTL-DATA-02, CTL-AUD-03  |

| MANAGE 3.1   | AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | CTL-EVAL-05, CTL-SUP-01               |
| MANAGE 4.1   | Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management.                                                                                                                                                                             | CTL-HUM-03, CTL-OBS-01                |

### NIST AI 600-1, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework — Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile

Registry id `nist-ai-600-1`, edition of 2024-07. Source: <https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1>.

**4 of 213 suggested actions referenced; 209 not assessed.** Action text copied from the NIST PDF. The 213 is a count of unique GV-/MP-/MS-/MG-n.n-nnn ids in the PDF (GV 59, MP 39, MS 72, MG 43), including GV-4.3-001, which the PDF prints as "GV4.3--001".

| Clause     | Text                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Controls    |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| MS-2.5-001 | Avoid extrapolating GAI system performance or capabilities from narrow, non-systematic, and anecdotal assessments.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | CTL-EVAL-01 |
| MS-2.7-001 | Apply established security measures to: Assess likelihood and magnitude of vulnerabilities and threats such as backdoors, compromised dependencies, data breaches, eavesdropping, man-in-the-middle attacks, reverse engineering, autonomous agents, model theft or exposure of model weights, AI inference, bypass, extraction, and other baseline security concerns. | CTL-SUP-01  |
| MS-2.7-007 | Perform AI red-teaming to assess resilience against: Abuse to facilitate attacks on other systems (e.g., malicious code generation, enhanced phishing content), GAI attacks (e.g., prompt injection), ML attacks (e.g., adversarial examples/prompts, data poisoning, membership inference, model extraction, sponge examples).                                        | CTL-MEM-02  |
| MS-2.8-003 | Use digital content transparency solutions to enable the documentation of each instance where content is generated, modified, or shared to provide a tamper-proof history of the content, promote transparency, and enable traceability. Robust version control systems can also be applied to track changes across the AI lifecycle over time.                        | CTL-AUD-01  |

| LLM10:2025 | Unbounded Consumption — "occurs when a Large Language Model (LLM) application allows users to conduct excessive and uncontrolled inferences, leading to risks such as denial of service (DoS), economic losses, model theft, and service degradation." | CTL-COST-01                          |
